headline: Recovery day, not a training day — HRV, body battery and sleep are all flashing red, and the easy run already on the calendar is the right call.
body_state: Readiness verdict is **red** at 29.4 (low band), driven by RHR. HRV last night was 36ms, below your normal band. Body Battery bottomed at **9** overnight — a morning under 30 means recovery didn't happen. You're carrying 26h of 14-day sleep debt and last night was only 5.4h. RHR sits at 54 vs your 49.9 baseline. Illness watch flags `rhr_elevated` + `hrv_below` but stays at level none, and skin temp is normal (+0.1°C) — this reads as under-recovery, not sickness.
session: Today's plan already has a **7km Easy Run @ 4:51–5:20/km** — no edit needed, the schedule matched the fatigue signal before this brief did. Run it truly conversational (RPE 3-4): if pace drifts slow to hold that effort, let it. Don't chase yesterday's tempo pace or Wednesday's Un1t intensity into this session.
recent: The last three days show why grey-zone training is your #1 limiter: Aug 11 stacked an Un1t class with a 2h hilly bike ride, Aug 12's scheduled 4km tempo landed at only 78% of planned volume (yellow) with HR topping 156 and averaging 143 — 20bpm under your 163 threshold despite RPE 8, a classic hard-feeling-but-not-actually-hard fatigue signal — and Aug 13's Un1t ran another 52% zone-3 session on top of it. None of these were true easy days, and that's exactly the pattern the readiness crash is punishing today.
focus: Keep today genuinely easy — cap effort by feel, not pace; the legs need a real recovery day before anything else works.
Protect sleep the next few nights (26h debt) ahead of the deload week starting Aug 17 — that's your natural reset point.
When quality resumes, spend it on the weakest HYROX stations (Row 1000m, Sandbag Lunges 100m, Sled Pull 50m) rather than adding more cross-training volume.
